question: What three major fields combine to form nursing informatics?

options.A: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.C: Clinical practice, software development, and physics
options.D: Public health, statistics, and hospital administration

explanation: Nursing informatics is a specialized field that integrates nursing knowledge with computer and information sciences to manage patient data effectively. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is the transition from paper records to digital platforms important in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for professional nurses
options.B: It increases the cost of delivering basic healthcare services
options.C: It reduces human error and secures patient data against physical loss
options.D: It makes doctors entirely responsible for patient documentation

explanation: Digital records protect sensitive health information from physical hazards like fire or water damage while minimizing documentation mistakes. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h1)

question: What primary device is most commonly used in mobile health interventions?
explanation: Mobile health relies heavily on portable handheld devices like smartphones and tablets to deliver care and access information anywhere. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h2)

question: A community health nurse wants to improve antenatal clinic attendance in a remote village. What is the best mHealth strategy to use?

options.A: Installing a complex electronic health record server in the village
options.B: Using video conferencing for every routine physical examination
options.C: Requiring all patients to buy personal laptop computers
options.D: Sending automated text message appointment reminders to pregnant women

explanation: Simple text messaging interventions are cost-effective and proven to boost appointment adherence in mobile health programs. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h2)

question: Continuous glucose monitors are best described as what type of device?

options.A: Sensors placed under the skin that transmit real-time blood sugar readings
options.B: Invasive surgical implants that replace pancreatic function entirely
options.C: Manual chemical test strips read visually by the patient
options.D: Large bedside machines used only in intensive care units

explanation: These wearable sensors provide continuous biochemical data directly to mobile devices without constant finger-pricking. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h3)

question: How do wearable devices change the nature of nursing assessments for chronic illness?

options.A: They shift all diagnostic responsibilities away from registered nurses
options.B: They replace the need for physical clinical examinations completely
options.C: They make patient vital signs completely invisible to healthcare providers
options.D: They provide continuous physiological data instead of isolated spot-checks

explanation: Continuous tracking captures trends over time, offering a clearer picture of health status than a single measurement taken at the clinic. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary difference between telehealth and telemedicine?

options.A: Telemedicine cannot be used by nurses, only by consultant physicians
options.B: Telehealth is restricted exclusively to urban teaching hospitals
options.C: Telemedicine focuses strictly on remote clinical diagnosis and treatment
options.D: Telehealth only involves administrative meetings between hospital managers

explanation: While telehealth is a broad term for all remote health services, telemedicine specifically targets clinical medical care delivered at a distance. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is a major nursing responsibility during a telehealth consultation?

options.A: Repairing faulty telecommunication satellite equipment during the call
options.B: Prescribing complex surgical procedures for the remote patient
options.C: Preparing the patient and ensuring accurate vital signs are transmitted
options.D: Acting as the sole legal owner of the patient digital record

explanation: Nurses facilitate virtual visits by getting the patient ready and providing reliable baseline clinical data to the remote provider. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary function of a Clinical Decision Support System?

options.A: Replacing nursing judgment with automated robotic patient care
options.B: Alerting staff to medication allergies and abnormal lab values
options.C: Designing new software applications for mobile smartphones
options.D: Managing hospital financial payroll and staff leave schedules

explanation: CDSS tools provide timely prompts and safety alerts directly within clinical workflows to protect patients from harm. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why must nurses apply critical thinking to AI-generated clinical recommendations?

options.A: Algorithms can sometimes generate false positives or incorrect suggestions
options.B: Computers are entirely incapable of processing medical data
options.C: Hospital management forbids nurses from using computer software
options.D: AI systems always remove the need for human documentation

explanation: Automated tools aid decision-making but do not replace professional clinical judgment and verification. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h5)

question: What does EHR stand for in healthcare technology?
explanation: EHR is the standard industry term for digital patient charts used in modern healthcare facilities. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h6)

question: What problem does interoperability solve in hospital information systems?

options.A: It eliminates the need for nurses to document patient care
options.B: It ensures different digital platforms can exchange data seamlessly
options.C: It prevents different software systems from sharing patient information
options.D: It increases the physical weight of paper charts in the ward

explanation: Interoperability allows separate healthcare technologies to communicate, preventing fragmented care and lost medical history. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge for nursing technology in Nigeria?

options.A: Erratic electricity supply and poor power infrastructure
options.B: Resistance to digital change among some experienced staff
options.C: Abundant, free, and flawless high-speed internet nationwide
options.D: High financial costs associated with software implementation

explanation: Reliable and free nationwide internet is far from reality; infrastructure deficits remain a major hurdle in many Nigerian facilities. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h7)

question: A nurse finishes reviewing patient lab results on a computer workstation in a busy ward. What is the immediate ethical action required?

options.A: Write down all patient passwords on a sticky note near the screen
options.B: Leave the workstation logged in for the next incoming shift
options.C: Log out of the terminal completely to protect patient confidentiality
options.D: Turn off the main electrical breaker for the entire hospital wing

explanation: Securing digital terminals prevents unauthorized access and upholds patient privacy rights mandated by professional codes of ethics. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h7)
